admission-controller.md.title: Admission Controller
admission-controller.md.summary: An Admission Controller intercepts requests to the Kubernetes API server before object persistence. These controllers can be validating, mutating, or both, and can reject or modify the requests.

admission-policies.md.title: Validating and Mutating Admission Policies
admission-policies.md.summary: This document explains declarative admission policies in Kubernetes, detailing Validating and Mutating types. It covers policy elements, CEL expressions, and how to test and modify these policies.

admission-webhooks-good-practices.md.title: Admission Webhook Good Practices
admission-webhooks-good-practices.md.summary: This document outlines best practices for designing and implementing admission webhooks in Kubernetes. It covers considerations for performance, preventing loops, managing mutations, and ensuring compatibility across API version upgrades.

affinity.md.title: Kubernetes Affinity Rules
affinity.md.summary: Affinity in Kubernetes provides rules to guide the scheduler on where to place pods. It includes node affinity and pod-to-pod affinity, which are defined using Kubernetes labels and selectors.

aggregation-layer.md.title: Aggregation Layer
aggregation-layer.md.summary: The aggregation layer allows users to install additional Kubernetes-style APIs in a cluster. It enables adding `APIService` objects to claim specific URL paths within the Kubernetes API.

annotation.md.title: Annotation Definition
annotation.md.summary: An annotation is a key-value pair used to attach arbitrary, non-identifying metadata to objects. This metadata can be small, large, structured, or unstructured, and can include various characters.

api-group.md.title: Kubernetes API Group
api-group.md.summary: An API group is a set of related paths within the Kubernetes API. It allows for easier extension of the Kubernetes API by enabling or disabling specific groups.

api-resource.md.title: API Resource
api-resource.md.summary: An API resource is an entity in the Kubernetes type system corresponding to an endpoint on the Kubernetes API. It defines the schema for objects or operations on that specific resource.

api-server-bypass-risks.md.title: Kubernetes API Server Bypass Risks
api-server-bypass-risks.md.summary: This document describes ways security controls in the Kubernetes API server can be bypassed, focusing on static Pods and the kubelet API. It guides operators on restricting these bypasses to maintain cluster security.

app-container.md.title: App Container Definition
app-container.md.summary: Application containers are the containers within a pod that start after any init containers have finished. Init containers are used to handle initialization tasks that are separate from the main application.

application-architect.md.title: Application Architect
application-architect.md.summary: An Application Architect is responsible for the high-level design of an application. They ensure the implementation allows the application to interact with surrounding components in a scalable and maintainable manner.

application-security-checklist.md.title: Application Security Checklist
application-security-checklist.md.summary: This document provides a checklist of basic guidelines for securing applications running in Kubernetes from a developer's perspective. It covers areas like application design, service accounts, and container security contexts.

approver.md.title: Approver Role in Kubernetes Code Contributions
approver.md.summary: The Approver is a role responsible for reviewing and approving Kubernetes code contributions. Approval involves a holistic acceptance check covering compatibility, conventions, performance, and system interactions.

architecture.md.title: Kubernetes Cluster Architecture
architecture.md.summary: This document outlines the necessary components for a complete Kubernetes cluster, detailing the roles of the control plane and worker nodes. It explains how these components work together to manage Pods and cluster operations.

authentication-mechanisms.md.title: Hardening Guide - Authentication Mechanisms
authentication-mechanisms.md.summary: This guide advises on selecting appropriate authentication mechanisms for Kubernetes clusters. It discusses the pros and cons of various built-in methods to help secure user access effectively.

authorization.md.title: Kubernetes Authorization
authorization.md.summary: This document explains how Kubernetes authorization works by evaluating request attributes against policies within the API server. Access is denied by default, and decisions are made sequentially by configured authorization modules.

autoscaling.md.title: Autoscaling Workloads
autoscaling.md.summary: This document explains how to scale workloads in Kubernetes, covering manual scaling, horizontal scaling using HPA, and vertical scaling using VPA. It details various methods for adapting workloads to resource demand.

cadvisor.md.title: cAdvisor
cadvisor.md.summary: cAdvisor is a daemon that provides container users with insights into the resource usage and performance of running containers. It collects, aggregates, and exports information such as resource isolation parameters and historical usage statistics.

cdi.md.title: Container Device Interface (CDI)
cdi.md.summary: CDI is a specification defining how to configure devices inside containers. Kubernetes uses CDI with device plugins and dynamic resource allocation to provide device setups like bind mounts or environment variables to workloads.

cel.md.title: Common Expression Language (CEL)
cel.md.summary: CEL is a general-purpose, fast, portable, and safe expression language. It is used in Kubernetes for running queries and performing fine-grained filtering on requests and resources.

certificate.md.title: Kubernetes Certificate
certificate.md.summary: A certificate is a cryptographically secure file used to validate access to a Kubernetes cluster. These certificates ensure that applications within the cluster can securely access the Kubernetes API.

cgroup.md.title: cgroup (control group)
cgroup.md.summary: cgroup is a Linux kernel feature that allows for the resource isolation, accounting, and limiting of resource usage for a group of processes. It manages CPU, memory, disk I/O, and network usage.

cidr.md.title: CIDR Notation in Networking
cidr.md.summary: CIDR is a notation used to describe blocks of IP addresses in networking. It is particularly used in Kubernetes to assign IP address ranges to Nodes for Pod allocation.

cla.md.title: Contributor License Agreement (CLA)
cla.md.summary: A CLA outlines the terms under which a contributor grants a license to an open-source project for their contributions. It is used to resolve legal disputes concerning contributed material and intellectual property.

cloud-controller-manager.md.title: Cloud Controller Manager
cloud-controller-manager.md.summary: The Cloud Controller Manager is a Kubernetes control plane component that embeds cloud-specific control logic. It links the cluster to a cloud provider's API, separating cloud interaction logic from core Kubernetes cluster components.

cloud-native-security.md.title: Cloud Native Security and Kubernetes
cloud-native-security.md.summary: This document outlines cloud-native information security practices across the development, distribution, deployment, and runtime lifecycle phases. It provides guidance on securing applications and the software supply chain within a Kubernetes environment.

cloud-provider.md.title: Cloud Provider Definition and Services
cloud-provider.md.summary: This document defines a cloud provider as an entity offering cloud computing platforms and services. It explains different service models like IaaS and PaaS, detailing the responsibilities of the provider in managing infrastructure and Kubernetes.

cluster-administration.md.title: Cluster Administration
cluster-administration.md.summary: This document guides users on planning, managing, and securing Kubernetes clusters. It covers considerations for setup, node management, and various security mechanisms.

cluster-operations.md.title: Kubernetes Cluster Operations
cluster-operations.md.summary: This document describes the work involved in managing a Kubernetes cluster, including day-to-day operations and coordinating upgrades. It outlines tasks such as scaling, upgrades, security implementation, and networking configuration.

cluster-operator.md.title: Cluster Operator
cluster-operator.md.summary: A Cluster Operator is a person responsible for configuring, controlling, and monitoring clusters. Their main duty is ensuring the cluster remains operational through maintenance and upgrades.

cluster.md.title: Cluster Definition
cluster.md.summary: A cluster is a set of worker machines (nodes) that run containerized applications. The control plane manages these nodes and the Pods, ensuring fault-tolerance and high availability.

cncf.md.title: Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF)
cncf.md.summary: The CNCF builds sustainable ecosystems and a community around projects that orchestrate containers in microservices architectures. It aims to make cloud native computing ubiquitous.

cni.md.title: Container Network Interface (CNI)
cni.md.summary: CNI plugins are a type of network plugin that follows the appc/CNI specification. This document provides an introduction to CNI plugins within the context of container networking.

components.md.title: Kubernetes Components
components.md.summary: This document provides a high-level overview of the essential components of a Kubernetes cluster, detailing the control plane, node components, and optional addons.

condition.md.title: Kubernetes Resource Conditions
condition.md.summary: A condition is a field in a Kubernetes resource's status that describes its current state. Conditions standardize how Kubernetes components communicate the status of resources using a type, status, reason, and message.

configuration.md.title: Kubernetes Configuration Mechanisms
configuration.md.summary: This document explains how Kubernetes separates configuration from code using APIs like ConfigMaps and Secrets. It also details methods for injecting configuration via sidecar or init containers.

container-env-variables.md.title: Container Environment Variables
container-env-variables.md.summary: Container environment variables are name=value pairs used to supply useful information to containers running in a pod. They provide necessary details for applications and important information about the container and related cluster resources.

container-runtime.md.title: Container Runtime
container-runtime.md.summary: The container runtime is a fundamental component that enables Kubernetes to effectively manage the execution and lifecycle of containers. It supports various runtimes that adhere to the Kubernetes CRI.

container.md.title: Container
container.md.summary: A container is a lightweight, portable executable image that bundles software and its dependencies. It decouples applications from the host infrastructure to simplify deployment and scaling.

containerd.md.title: containerd
containerd.md.summary: containerd is a container runtime designed for simplicity, robustness, and portability. It handles tasks such as fetching and storing images, executing containers, and managing network access.

containers.md.title: Containers: Images and Runtimes
containers.md.summary: This document discusses containers, container images, and container runtimes. It explains that containers decouple applications from infrastructure and that images are immutable software packages.

contributor.md.title: Contributor Definition
contributor.md.summary: This document defines what a contributor is within the Kubernetes project or community. It outlines the types of contributions individuals can make to the project.

control-plane.md.title: Control Plane
control-plane.md.summary: The Control Plane is the container orchestration layer responsible for exposing APIs and interfaces to define, deploy, and manage the lifecycle of containers. It is composed of various components that manage the orchestration process.

cpu-constraint-namespace.md.title: Configure Minimum and Maximum CPU Constraints for a Namespace
cpu-constraint-namespace.md.summary: This document explains how to set minimum and maximum CPU resource constraints for Pods within a Kubernetes namespace using a LimitRange object. It details how these constraints enforce resource requests and limits on containers.

cpu-default-namespace.md.title: Configure Default CPU Requests and Limits for a Namespace
cpu-default-namespace.md.summary: This document explains how to configure default CPU requests and limits for a Kubernetes namespace using a LimitRange. It details how the control plane assigns these defaults to containers within a Pod.

cri-o.md.title: CRI-O
cri-o.md.summary: CRI-O is a tool that enables the use of OCI container runtimes with Kubernetes CRI. It allows Kubernetes to utilize any OCI-compliant runtime for running Pods and fetching container images from remote registries.

cron-jobs.md.title: CronJob Documentation
cron-jobs.md.summary: This document explains how to use CronJobs to create Jobs that run on a repeating schedule. It details the Cron syntax for scheduling and discusses limitations and configuration options.

csi.md.title: Container Storage Interface (CSI)
csi.md.summary: The Container Storage Interface (CSI) defines a standard interface for exposing storage systems to containers. It enables vendors to create custom, out-of-tree storage plugins for Kubernetes.

customresourcedefinition.md.title: CustomResourceDefinition
customresourcedefinition.md.summary: A CustomResourceDefinition (CRD) is an API object used to define a new custom API for the Kubernetes API server. It allows users to extend the built-in Kubernetes API to meet specific environmental needs.

daemonset.md.title: DaemonSet
daemonset.md.summary: A DaemonSet ensures that a copy of a Pod runs on every (or some) node in the cluster. It manages the lifecycle of these Pods based on node presence.

debug-application.md.title: Troubleshooting Applications
debug-application.md.summary: This document provides resources for fixing issues with containerized applications. It covers common problems with Kubernetes resources and methods for debugging running containers.

debug-cluster.md.title: Troubleshooting Clusters
debug-cluster.md.summary: This document guides users through troubleshooting Kubernetes clusters, focusing on listing nodes, debugging unreachable nodes, examining logs, and understanding cluster failure modes.

debug.md.title: Monitoring, Logging, and Debugging Guide
debug.md.summary: This guide provides resources for debugging applications and clusters in Kubernetes, including sections on logging, monitoring, and community help channels.

deployment.md.title: Kubernetes Deployments Overview
deployment.md.summary: This document explains how Kubernetes Deployments provide declarative updates for Pods and ReplicaSets. It covers creating, updating, rolling back, scaling, and managing the status of deployments.

device-plugin.md.title: Device Plugin
device-plugin.md.summary: Device plugins run on worker nodes to provide Pods with access to infrastructure resources, like local hardware, that need vendor-specific setup. They advertise these resources to the kubelet so workloads can utilize hardware features.

device-plugins.md.title: Device Plugins
device-plugins.md.summary: This document describes the Kubernetes device plugin framework, allowing vendors to advertise system hardware resources like GPUs or NICs. It details the registration process, implementation workflow, and integration with the kubelet.

device.md.title: Device Definition
device.md.summary: A device is an infrastructure resource directly or indirectly attached to your nodes. These can range from commercial products like GPUs to custom hardware such as ASIC boards, often requiring device drivers for Kubernetes Pods to access them.

deviceclass.md.title: DeviceClass
deviceclass.md.summary: DeviceClass is a category of cluster devices used with dynamic resource allocation (DRA). Administrators use them to define sets of devices that can be claimed for use in workloads.

disruption.md.title: Kubernetes Pod Disruption
disruption.md.summary: This document defines disruptions as events causing Pods to go out of service, impacting workload management resources. It distinguishes between voluntary and involuntary disruptions based on the cause of the Pod going offline.

dns-pod-service.md.title: DNS for Services and Pods
dns-pod-service.md.summary: This document explains how Kubernetes creates DNS records for Services and Pods to enable service discovery. It details record types like A/AAAA and SRV records and how namespace scoping affects DNS resolution.

docker.md.title: Docker Engine and Containers
docker.md.summary: Docker is a software technology that provides operating-system-level virtualization through containers. It utilizes Linux kernel features like cgroups and namespaces to allow independent containers to run efficiently on a single host.

dockershim.md.title: Dockershim
dockershim.md.summary: Dockershim is a component in Kubernetes versions up to 1.23 that enables the kubelet to communicate with the Docker Engine. It has been removed from Kubernetes starting with version 1.24.

downstream.md.title: Downstream (disambiguation)
downstream.md.summary: This document clarifies the usage of the term 'downstream' within the Kubernetes ecosystem. It explains that it refers to code or tools that depend on the core Kubernetes codebase or a forked repository.

downward-api.md.title: Downward API
downward-api.md.summary: The Downward API allows containers to consume information about themselves or the cluster without coupling to the Kubernetes client. It provides methods to expose Pod and container fields via environment variables or downwardAPI volumes.

drain.md.title: Pod Drain Process
drain.md.summary: This document explains the process of safely evicting Pods from a Node to prepare it for maintenance or removal from a cluster. It details the use of the `kubectl drain` command for this purpose.

dual-stack.md.title: IPv4/IPv6 dual-stack
dual-stack.md.summary: This document explains how to enable and configure IPv4/IPv6 dual-stack networking in Kubernetes clusters. It details the supported features, prerequisites, and configuration steps for Pods and Services.

duration.md.title: Kubernetes Duration Format
duration.md.summary: This document explains how duration values are represented in Kubernetes APIs. It details the format using non-negative integers combined with specific time unit suffixes.

dynamic-volume-provisioning.md.title: Dynamic Volume Provisioning
dynamic-volume-provisioning.md.summary: This document explains dynamic volume provisioning, which allows users to request the automatic creation of storage volumes. It eliminates the need for administrators to pre-provision storage by automatically provisioning based on user requests.

endpoint-slice.md.title: EndpointSlice
endpoint-slice.md.summary: EndpointSlices track the IP addresses of backend endpoints, typically associated with a Service and representing Pods. The control plane usually manages these automatically, but they can be defined manually.

endpoint-slices.md.title: EndpointSlices
endpoint-slices.md.summary: EndpointSlices in Kubernetes contain references to network endpoints, grouping them by IP family, protocol, port, and Service name. They serve as the source of truth for kube-proxy regarding internal traffic routing.

endpoint.md.title: Endpoints API Deprecation
endpoint.md.summary: This document discusses the deprecated API for representing the set of all endpoints for a Service. Kubernetes now uses EndpointSlices instead of the original Endpoints API due to scalability concerns.

ephemeral-container.md.title: Ephemeral Container
ephemeral-container.md.summary: An ephemeral container is a container type that can be temporarily run inside a pod for diagnostic purposes. They lack resource guarantees and should not be used for running the main workload.

etcd.md.title: etcd
etcd.md.summary: etcd is a consistent and highly-available key-value store that serves as the backing store for all cluster data in Kubernetes. It provides the foundational data storage for Kubernetes clusters.

event.md.title: Kubernetes Events
event.md.summary: Kubernetes Events are objects that describe state changes or notable occurrences within the cluster. They should be treated as informative, best-effort, supplemental data.

eviction.md.title: Eviction
eviction.md.summary: Eviction is the process of terminating one or more Pods on Nodes. It describes the two main types of eviction: Node-pressure eviction and API-initiated eviction.

extend-kubernetes.md.title: Extending Kubernetes
extend-kubernetes.md.summary: This guide describes methods for customizing Kubernetes clusters, focusing primarily on extensions. It explains how to adapt Kubernetes to specific work environment needs through various extension points and patterns.

extensions.md.title: Kubernetes Extensions
extensions.md.summary: Extensions are software components that deeply integrate with Kubernetes to support new types of hardware. Most users benefit from pre-installed extensions in hosted or distribution Kubernetes clusters.

feature-gates.md.title: Feature Gate
feature-gates.md.summary: Feature gates are opaque string values used to control which Kubernetes features are enabled in a cluster. They can be enabled or disabled using the `--feature-gates` command line flag on Kubernetes components.

finalizer.md.title: Kubernetes Finalizers
finalizer.md.summary: Finalizers are namespaced keys that instruct Kubernetes to wait for specific conditions before deleting resources. They allow controllers to clean up associated resources before the object is fully removed.

flexvolume.md.title: FlexVolume Interface Deprecation
flexvolume.md.summary: FlexVolume is a deprecated interface for creating out-of-tree volume plugins. It allows users to write custom drivers for volumes in Kubernetes, but it has limitations.

gateway.md.title: Gateway API Overview
gateway.md.summary: The Gateway API provides an extensible, role-oriented configuration mechanism for making network services available. It defines API kinds like GatewayClass, Gateway, HTTPRoute, and GRPCRoute for dynamic infrastructure provisioning and advanced traffic routing.

glossary-api-eviction.md.title: API-initiated Eviction
glossary-api-eviction.md.summary: This document explains how to use the Eviction API to create an Eviction object, which triggers graceful pod termination. API-initiated evictions respect configured PodDisruptionBudgets and termination grace periods.

glossary-configmap.md.title: ConfigMap
glossary-configmap.md.summary: A ConfigMap is an API object used to store non-confidential data in key-value pairs. It allows decoupling environment-specific configuration from container images for easier portability.

glossary-container-lifecycle-hooks.md.title: Container Lifecycle Hooks
glossary-container-lifecycle-hooks.md.summary: This document explains container lifecycle hooks, which allow users to execute code at specific points in the container management lifecycle. It details two available hooks: PostStart and PreStop.

glossary-controller.md.title: Kubernetes Controllers
glossary-controller.md.summary: Controllers in Kubernetes are control loops that monitor the cluster state and initiate necessary changes to move the current state toward the desired state. They watch the cluster state via the API server and some run within the control plane.

glossary-cri.md.title: Container Runtime Interface (CRI)
glossary-cri.md.summary: The CRI is the main protocol used for communication between the kubelet and the container runtime. It defines the gRPC protocol for this interaction.

glossary-deployment.md.title: Deployment Overview
glossary-deployment.md.summary: A Deployment manages a replicated application by running stateless Pods distributed across cluster nodes. It is the primary object for managing replicated applications in a cluster.

glossary-downward-api.md.title: Downward API
glossary-downward-api.md.summary: The Downward API is Kubernetes' mechanism for exposing Pod and container field values to code running inside a container. It allows containers to access self-information or cluster context without directly coupling them to the Kubernetes API.

glossary-dra.md.title: Dynamic Resource Allocation
glossary-dra.md.summary: Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) is a Kubernetes feature enabling the request and sharing of resources like hardware accelerators among Pods. It works by defining device classes for devices and allocating matching devices to workload claims on appropriate nodes.

glossary-garbage-collection.md.title: Garbage Collection
glossary-garbage-collection.md.summary: Garbage collection in Kubernetes refers to the mechanisms used to clean up cluster resources. This process handles removing unused containers, failed Pods, orphaned objects, completed Jobs, and expired resources.
topics: objects owned by the targeted resource
resources that have expired or failed

glossary-kube-scheduler.md.title: kube-scheduler
glossary-kube-scheduler.md.summary: The kube-scheduler is a control plane component responsible for watching for Pods without an assigned node and selecting an appropriate node for them. It considers various factors like resource requirements, constraints, and affinity rules to make scheduling decisions.

glossary-kubectl.md.title: Kubectl
glossary-kubectl.md.summary: Kubectl is a command-line tool used to communicate with a Kubernetes cluster's control plane via the Kubernetes API. It allows users to perform operations such as creating, inspecting, updating, and deleting Kubernetes objects.

glossary-kubernetes-api.md.title: Kubernetes API
glossary-kubernetes-api.md.summary: The Kubernetes API is the HTTP interface enabling communication between users, cluster components, and external entities. It allows users to query and manipulate the state of Kubernetes objects through RESTful calls.

glossary-logging.md.title: Logging
glossary-logging.md.summary: Logs are lists of events recorded by a cluster or application. These logs are essential for debugging issues and monitoring cluster activity.

glossary-mixed-version-proxy.md.title: Mixed Version Proxy (MVP)
glossary-mixed-version-proxy.md.summary: The Mixed Version Proxy (MVP) allows a kube-apiserver to proxy resource requests to a different peer API server. This feature ensures that resource requests are served by the correct API server when multiple Kubernetes API server versions coexist in a cluster.

glossary-node-pressure-eviction.md.title: Node-pressure eviction
glossary-node-pressure-eviction.md.summary: Node-pressure eviction is the kubelet's process to proactively terminate pods on nodes to reclaim resources. This is triggered when monitored resources like CPU, memory, disk space, or inodes reach specific consumption levels.

glossary-pod-lifecycle.md.title: Pod Lifecycle
glossary-pod-lifecycle.md.summary: This document describes the sequence of states a Pod passes through during its lifetime. It defines five possible Pod phases: Pending, Running, Succeeded, Failed, and Unknown.

glossary-pod-security-policy.md.title: Pod Security Policy
glossary-pod-security-policy.md.summary: Pod Security Policy was a former Kubernetes API used to enforce security restrictions on pod creation and updates. It has been deprecated and removed in recent Kubernetes versions.

glossary-secret.md.title: Managing Secrets in Systems
glossary-secret.md.summary: This document explains how to store sensitive information like passwords and tokens securely. It details how secrets can be referenced by Pods and distinguishes them from ConfigMaps for non-confidential data.

glossary-security-context.md.title: Security Context
glossary-security-context.md.summary: The securityContext field defines privilege and access control settings for a Pod or container. It allows configuration of the user, group, privileges, and security policies.
